prompt:
Paint ONE finished frame of a film-like cutscene of our hand-painted point-and-click adventure game 'Posledny zvonec' (Slovakia; eras 1960, 1982, 1995, 2020, 2035). The reference images are numbered in the order they are given: Image 1: the chronochamber from the previous frames (keep the table, window and light) Image 2: character reference: Viktor, 50 Image 3: character reference: Nina, 30, who appears on a small video screen

Shot: Medium close shot: Viktor sits at the plain table and signs a printed incident report with a pen, unhurried, serious, alone. On the table a small tablet stands on a stand, showing Nina on a video call, watching him, matter-of-fact. The glass of water. No crowd, no applause.

Characters in this frame (briefs of the approved designs): Viktor, a 50-year-old Slovak founder of the Atlas archive in June 2035: controlled and convinced, grieving underneath; he has not slept. Short dark hair greying at the temples, slightly unkempt, a day of dark stubble, tired eyes with faint shadows under them, a serious composed face, lean build. He wears a plain white cotton dress shirt, collar open with no tie, sleeves rolled up to the elbows, slightly creased, tucked into dark charcoal trousers with a black belt, and black leather shoes; a plain steel wristwatch. His arms hang at his sides. An ordinary man in ordinary clothes: not a villain, not a caricature, no futuristic uniform, no lab coat, no face mask. Nina, a 30-year-old Slovak woman, curator of the Atlas memory exhibition in June 2035 and Ela's daughter: matter-of-fact, quick, clear about the limits of her authority. Straight dark brown hair, shoulder-length, worn loose with a side part and tucked behind one ear, a sharp intelligent face with a direct gaze. She wears a lightweight unlined dark bottle-green knee-length coat, open and unbuttoned, over a plain light grey crew-neck top, slim black trousers and simple white leather trainers. A service identification card hangs on a plain dark grey lanyard around her neck: a white card with a small photo square and a simple blue circle emblem, no readable text. Her arms hang relaxed at her sides. Ordinary clothes of the near future (alpine summer 2035), nothing futuristic, no logos, no face mask.

Light and time: Bright mountain daylight from the window now, calmer and clearer than before.

Character references show approved characters of the game on a plain grey card: copy each person's face, age, hair, body proportions, clothes and colours exactly, but pose and light them for this scene; never copy the grey card, the sheet layout or a duplicate of the same person. Place references show the real location and its painted version in our game: keep its architecture, materials and era. Photos are only references: repaint everything in our style, paint any real people in them out, and do not copy brand logos or shop names. Composition: a cinematic 16:9 film frame with a clear focal point and depth (foreground, subject, background), painted full-bleed to all four edges (never paint black letterbox bars or a border: the game adds its own bars later and they cover the top tenth and the bottom fifth of the image, with the subtitles), so keep faces, hands and the key object inside the middle band. One single image: no panels, no split screen, no border, no frame, no captions, no subtitles, no speech bubbles, no watermark, no UI, unless the shot asks for it. No text or lettering anywhere unless the shot quotes it exactly.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
